items.stem: In design thinking, what is the main goal of the Empathise mode?

options.text: To understand users' real needs and context before defining solutions
options.rationale: Correct: empathy work grounds the whole process in genuine user needs.
Visual decisions come much later, if at all, in this mode.
Building comes after problems are framed and tested.
Budgeting is a management task, not the purpose of empathising.

items.explanation: Correct: empathy work grounds the whole process in genuine user needs.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when interviewing users? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: open questions surface real behaviour rather than confirming assumptions.

options.text: Listen more than you talk and probe for stories
options.rationale: Correct: concrete stories reveal needs better than opinions.

options.text: Suggest the answer you hope to hear

options.rationale: Closed questions limit the insight you can gather.

items.explanation: Correct: open questions surface real behaviour rather than confirming assumptions.

items.stem: A usability test shows users repeatedly miss a key button. What does this most directly indicate?

options.text: A usability problem to fix, regardless of how the screen looks
options.rationale: Correct: observed task failure is direct evidence of a usability issue.

options.text: That the users are not smart enough
options.rationale: UX blames the design, not the user, for consistent failures.

options.text: That the colour scheme is perfect
options.rationale: Missing a button is a usability failure, not a win.

options.text: That no further testing is needed
options.rationale: Findings should drive iteration and re-testing.

items.explanation: Correct: observed task failure is direct evidence of a usability issue.
